correctness.rationale: Hub-zero rim update is \(y_i=x_{i-1}x_{i+1}\). With hub fixed, two steps give \(x_i=x_{i-2}x_ix_{i+2}\), forcing unions of step-two components; hub-majority constraints leave only unanimity and, for even rims, four alternating-rim states. With the hub flipping, the second step gives \(x_i=x_i(x_{i-2}\lor x_{i+2})\), equivalent to no isolated ones in step-two components, and the two hub changes are exactly \(2m>n\) and \(2e<n\). Labeled cyclic-run counting with b positive runs gives the \(Q_L\) coefficients, including the doubled length-two step graph, and partitioning by the hub yields the \(T_n\) and \(B_n\) formulas. Goles–Olivos provides the general period-one-or-two restriction. Executed exact verifier compares full dynamics \(3\le n\le15\), independent four-state polynomial transfer \(2\le L\le28\), and coefficient counts \(3\le n\le60\).

value.rationale: Wheel graphs are a natural universal-hub social-network family and a minimal departure from the cycle. The exact structural census demonstrates only two stationary colorings but exponentially many strict oscillating attractors for infinitely many rim sizes; it distinguishes constant-hub parity oscillators from hub-switching oscillators and gives an exact polynomial-time all-size count. This addresses a motivated full-graph invariant beyond small enumeration or a general period theorem.
